title: Independent reproduction record
description: One record per independent reproduction: someone unaffiliated with this project took a released artifact, ran it on their own hardware, and published what they got. That is E6_INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCED, the top of the ladder in src/validation/evidenceLevel.ts, and the one level this project can never award itself. Validated by scripts/verify-reproduction-record.mjs, which refuses a record whose reproducer turns out to be us. NOTHING IN THIS DIRECTORY IS A REPRODUCTION: it holds one EXAMPLE record and nobody outside this project has reproduced anything.

recordId.description: Stable identity. An example must be prefixed EXAMPLE- and carry example: true.

evidenceLevelClaimed.description: This container is E6 and holds nothing else. A run by this project, however careful, is not a reproduction and belongs nowhere in here.

claimIds.description: The claims this reproduction bears on. Each must exist in docs/validation/claim-register.yaml, which the verifier reads and never writes.

outcome.description: Present only when the reproducer actually ran something and reported numbers.

reproducer.description: Who did it, in a form a third party can look up. A name alone is not identity: an ORCID, a ROR, or another persistent identifier is what lets a reader check that the reproducer exists and is not us.

contact.description: How the reproducer can be reached to confirm the record. Optional, because a persistent identifier already carries that, and because a record should not force a private address into a public file.

independence.description: The three ways a reproduction stops being one. All three are stated, all three are checked, and any of them being true is a refusal rather than a caveat.

statement.description: In the reproducer's own words: their relationship to this project, or the absence of one.

artifactUnderTest.description: Exactly what they ran, pinned. A reproduction of an unspecified build reproduces nothing.

downloadUrl.description: Where they got it. https, and a host somebody else can reach.

executed.description: What they actually ran, as commands, not as a description of what they intended.

environment.description: The hardware and runtime it ran on. Different hardware is most of what a reproduction is for: a result that only appears on the author's laptop is not a result.

runtime.description: Node version, browser build, or whatever executed the code.

comparedAgainst.description: What their numbers were held against: a published figure, a release manifest digest, a claim register entry.

deviations.description: Every place their result differed. An empty array is a positive statement that there were none, and is only credible next to a raw output someone can read.

rawOutput.description: Where the reproducer's own output lives, under their control, not ours. A reproduction whose evidence exists only inside this repository is a claim about a third party that the third party cannot be checked against.

publishedBy.description: Who controls the location. A reproduction published by this project is a copy of someone's claim, not their record.

scope.description: What was reproduced and what was not. notReproduced may never be empty: a reproduction that states no boundary reads as covering the whole product.
